rejected.title: Magna Carta
card: In 1215, King John of England was unpopular with his barons, the powerful nobles who held land from the king. They disliked his heavy taxes and his unfair treatment of them, such as large fines and taking their land.
The barons rebelled and forced John to agree to a written charter called Magna Carta, which is Latin for "Great Charter".
The charter said the king was also under the law. He could not simply do as he pleased: he had to follow the law and the charter's terms.
Magna Carta was an early limit on a ruler's power. Later generations looked back on it when they argued that rulers must obey the law.
rejected.remember: Magna Carta made the king answer to the law, an early limit on a ruler's power.

a.q: What was the main idea in Magna Carta, agreed in 1215?
opts: The king was also under the law
The king would share his land equally
The barons would pay no more taxes ever
The king would rule England without nobles
a.why: Magna Carta said the king was under the law and had to keep to the charter's terms, which limited his power. The barons wanted limits on John's behaviour, not to end the monarchy or to remove all taxes.
a.clue: Think about who the barons wanted to hold to the rules.

b.q: Why is Magna Carta seen as important in the history of limits on rulers' power?
opts: It said a king must obey the law, an early limit on power
It made the barons into the new kings of England
It was a gift from a king who wanted to give up power
It gave every English person a vote for the king
b.why: The barons forced John to accept that the king was under the law, so a ruler's power now had a limit. It did not make barons kings, and John agreed only because he was forced to, not as a gift.
b.clue: Remember who forced whom to agree.

problems.detail: "He had to follow the same rules as others" overstates Magna Carta. It bound the king to the law of the land and to the charter's terms, but it did not make him subject to the same rules as everyone. Many of its protections applied only to barons, the Church and free men, not to unfree peasants. Suggest: "he had to follow the law and the charter's terms."
The why says the king "had to follow the law like everyone else". This repeats the card's overstatement that Magna Carta put the king under the same rules as all his subjects.

version.title: Magna Carta
card: In 1215, King John of England was unpopular with his barons, the powerful nobles who held land from the king. They disliked his heavy taxes and his unfair treatment of them, such as large fines and taking their land.
The barons rebelled and forced John to agree to a written charter called Magna Carta, which is Latin for "Great Charter".
The charter said the king was also under the law. He could not simply do as he pleased: he had to follow the law and the charter's terms.
Magna Carta was an early limit on a ruler's power. Later generations looked back on it when they argued that rulers must obey the law.
version.remember: Magna Carta made the king answer to the law, an early limit on a ruler's power.

a.q: What did King John accept when he agreed to Magna Carta in 1215?
opts: That the king was under the law too
That he would share his land equally
That barons would never pay taxes again
That England would be ruled without nobles
a.why: Magna Carta said the king was under the law and had to keep to the charter's terms. The barons wanted limits on John's behaviour, such as his heavy taxes and fines, not an end to all taxes or to the nobles' role.
a.clue: Think about what the barons wanted John to follow.

b.q: Centuries after 1215, people angry at a king who jails critics without a trial look back to Magna Carta. What made it useful to them?
opts: It held that the king was bound by the law
It ended the power of kings in England
It let barons choose a new king each year
It gave every English person a vote for king
b.why: Magna Carta said even the king was under the law, so later generations used it to argue that rulers must obey the law. It did not end the monarchy: John stayed king, but he had to keep to the charter.
b.clue: Did John stop being king after 1215?

a.best: That the king was under the law too
